content: 1. The reduction in the incidence of air leaks, assessed through conditions such as pulmonary interstitial emphysema, pneumothorax, and pneumomediastinum, was estimated to be 38 fewer cases per 1,000 patients. However, the confidence interval ranged from 18 fewer to 53 fewer cases, and the quality of evidence was rated as low. 2. For air leak syndromes, the reduction was estimated at 7 fewer cases per 1,000 patients, with a confidence interval ranging from 30 fewer to 20 more cases. The quality of evidence for this outcome was rated as very low. 3. The studies reviewed were conducted in level-3 neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) located in high-income countries, with the exception of one study. 4. Data from studies with the lowest and highest control group risks were used to estimate the low and high control risks, respectively. 5. The outcomes assessed were subjective, and the blinding of outcome assessment was unclear, as it was not explicitly mentioned in any of the studies. 6. All studies, except one, were conducted in level-3 NICUs in high-income countries. 7. The 95% confidence interval around the pooled estimate of effect included both no effect and an increased risk, indicating uncertainty in the results. 8. One of the studies included in the analysis was conducted in a lowor middle-income country.
